question: Do any of the exact 168 previously screened rune-to-byte streams decode as a complete, bounded compressed stream?
targets: The same 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages and their joined stream, with no page or byte offset search.
strict_rule: Start at byte zero. Require decoder EOF and zero unused/trailing input bytes, and cap decompressed output at 1,048,576 bytes. Classify invalid, incomplete, trailing and output-limit separately. A valid decompression is not necessarily meaningful text.
controls: For each format, compress a fixed synthetic message and require full recovery; reject truncated and appended-junk versions. Test the one-megabyte output limit using a synthetic expansion. Try a deterministic rune-index five-bit fixture only if an exact compression stream can be represented using indices 0–28 and zero padding.
excluded: No scanning offsets or prefixes, guessed header bytes, alternative packing, changed page order, dictionary candidates, recursive decompression, unlimited output or language-based scoring.
